name: Lucida AI
product: Voice-first AI speaking coach app (iOS and Android) for practising spoken English and other languages; also sold to corporate teams.
pricing_model: Free download with an in-app subscription for some features; the company says prices vary by country and app store (exact prices not published).
expansion_signal: Says the seed money will fund expansion into new languages and new geographies, plus scaling its enterprise offering globally.
africa_use_case: Nigerian, Kenyan and Ghanaian students and job seekers preparing for IELTS-style speaking tests or English-language interviews could pay a monthly subscription for unlimited AI speaking practice funded via mobile money.
notes: Seed reached $7M after a $1.6M top-up (tech.eu); total raised about $8.25M per Tech Funding News. Other participants: Next Tier Ventures, Look AI Ventures, Bogazici Ventures, Yapi Kredi Frwrd Ventures, Unlu & Co. Strongest fit in this batch: English-speaking practice is a high-demand paid category across Anglophone and Francophone Africa.

name: Sekai
product: Social app where users describe an idea and an AI agent builds a playable mini-app (games, quizzes, interactive memes) that others can play and remix.
pricing_model: Free app with in-app purchases (App Store listing); price points not confirmed.
lead_investors: Series A co-led by Khosla Ventures (Keith Rabois) and Connect Ventures (Nicole Quinn); seed led by Mayfield (Navin Chaddha)
africa_use_case: Young African creators on TikTok and WhatsApp could buy in-app credits to build and share local-language quiz and game mini-apps for their audiences.
notes: Axios reported the $20M Series A on 2026-06-01; the combined $26M seed + Series A press release went out on GlobeNewswire on 2026-06-03. Company says users have built over 15 million mini-apps. Monetisation details are thin.

name: Tilt
product: Live-video auction marketplace app where independent sellers run real-time auctions (trading cards, collectibles and other goods), with AI tools that turn video frames into listings.
pricing_model: Free app; buyers pay per item won in auctions. Seller fee structure not found.
round_stage: Not found (reported as fresh funding; one outlet calls it Series B)
lead_investors: Not confirmed: sources conflict (FinSMEs names Vinted Ventures as lead; The BAE HQ names TQ Ventures). Existing investors include Balderton Capital, Earlybird and Seedcamp.
expansion_signal: Plans to expand its seller base across more European countries and into the United States.
africa_use_case: Collectors and small resellers in Lagos, Nairobi or Johannesburg could join live auctions and pay for won items in local currency instead of needing an international card.
notes: Founded by ex-Revolut staff (Tech Funding News). Total raised now over $50M per Startup Researcher. Fit is moderate: physical-goods shipping into Africa is a barrier, so the pitch is mainly buyer-side checkout.

name: Retro (Lone Palm Labs)
product: Friends-only photo-sharing app for weekly photo recaps, shared albums and memory 'rewinds', with no ads or algorithmic feed.
pricing_model: Free app with an in-app subscription (Retro Premium) for video/GIF comments, more styles and unlimited history; reported at $4.99/month or $35.99/year on the US App Store.
lead_investors: Field Ventures (Dylan Field) and Thrive Capital
africa_use_case: Families split between African cities and the diaspora could pay a few dollars a month for private shared albums and recaps without needing a card.
notes: CAVEAT: the round was disclosed in window (SEC Form D dated 2026-08-19; TechCrunch confirmation 2026-08-28), but TechCrunch says the money closed in December 2025. Pricing figure comes from viral.app citing TechCrunch. About 7M downloads per Appfigures (via TechCrunch).

name: Yope
product: Private, friends-only photo and video messaging app (lock-screen widgets, group walls, AI recaps) with no ads or public feed.
pricing_model: Free download with a monthly premium subscription (per 36Kr's app-store review); price not found.
round_stage: Seed / pre-Series A (sources differ on the label)
expansion_signal: Plans to use the round to grow the product and expand operations into the United States.
africa_use_case: Gen Z friend groups in African cities could buy Yope's premium tier through mobile-money-funded wallet payments, since many lack cards for app-store subscriptions.
notes: Tech Funding News describes Yope as London-based; Seedtable says the app is operated by Salo App, Inc., so legal domicile may be US. Other investors: Inovo, Redseed, Geek Ventures. Total funding about $20M.

name: Notey
product: Gamified music-practice platform: children play a real guitar while the game listens and adapts the curriculum; teachers can see practice between lessons.
pricing_model: Not found (has a parent-facing consumer offer; prices not confirmed).
lead_investors: Tivoli Ventures; co-led by Malta Venture Capital
expansion_signal: Opening a European operation in Malta and signing a distribution deal with telecom operator Telemach to reach households in the Balkans.
africa_use_case: Parents in South Africa, Nigeria and Kenya who pay for after-school music lessons could subscribe to guided guitar practice at a fraction of tutor cost.
founders: Mak Grgic, Adithya Bellathur, Yishai Pinchover
notes: The $3M includes a $1M non-dilutive grant from Malta Enterprise. Techstars 2023 alum. Offices in New York City, Columbia (South Carolina) and Valletta. Its telecom-distribution model suggests an African telco partnership could be a route in.

name: Jarvie AI
product: AI assistant you add to iMessage/SMS group chats to plan events and trips, summarise conversations, look up information and draft emails or calendar events.
expansion_signal: Plans to extend beyond iMessage to other messaging services (a product expansion; no geographic plan stated).
africa_use_case: If Jarvie reaches WhatsApp, African family, church and alumni groups could pay for a shared group-chat assistant that organises events and contributions.
notes: Operated by All Day Technologies, Inc. (API Evangelist). Fit stays low until it supports WhatsApp, because iMessage use in Africa is small. An App Store app called 'Jarvi' is a different product and was not used for pricing.

name: Botsi
product: AI monetisation platform that replaces static paywalls in mobile and web subscription apps with personalised, real-time offers and pricing.
lead_investors: Not found (participants: Telegraph Ventures, Plain Sight Capital, Atlanta Tech Angels, VentureSouth, angels)
africa_use_case: Indie subscription-app developers selling into Africa could use Botsi to show region-specific offers while Cozzipay handles local-currency checkout, which makes it a possible partner as well as a lead.
founders: Jacob Rushfinn, Jason Schubert, William Schubert
notes: B2B tool for app developers rather than a consumer product, so it suits a partnership or integration pitch more than a direct customer pitch. Founded 2025, New York-based.

name: Wayy.ai
product: Autonomous web app that acts as an AI 'sales co-founder' for solopreneurs and small businesses: finds prospects, runs outreach and automates sales workflows.
africa_use_case: African freelancers, agencies and SME founders selling services abroad could pay a monthly fee for automated lead generation and outreach.
notes: San Francisco-based, founded 2026. Launch press release on GlobeNewswire dated 2026-08-03. Strategic angel Tunc Yalgin participated.

name: Backgrounder
product: AI plus human-expert service that checks suspicious emails, texts, calls and social messages so individuals and SMBs can avoid scams and impersonation before sending money.
expansion_signal: None stated (funds go to product, team, and launching mobile apps and browser protection)
africa_use_case: Mobile-money users and small merchants in Kenya, Ghana and Nigeria, who are frequent targets of SIM-swap and impersonation scams, could pay a small monthly fee for scam checks.
notes: Arlington, Virginia. Other investors: Virginia Innovation Partnership Corporation, Skylab Capital, plus named angels. Consumer apps not yet launched, so it is early for a payments pitch.

name: Dapta
product: AI voice and text sales agent (Dapti) that instantly answers, qualifies and books inbound leads for small and medium businesses.
expansion_signal: Raising to expand across the United States and Latin America.
africa_use_case: African clinics, schools and real-estate agents that get WhatsApp and phone leads could pay monthly for an AI agent that answers and books them around the clock.
founders: Nicolas Rojas (CEO); other founders not found
notes: HQ in Scottsdale, Arizona and Miami (TheSaaSNews; Phoenix Business Journal); Colombian origins per Forbes Colombia. Other investors: Crew Capital, Broom Ventures, Cometa VC, 500 Global, Fen Ventures. Total raised $7.4M. Its emerging-market (LatAm) playbook may make it receptive to an Africa pitch.

name: Mostest
product: AI-driven event booking platform that connects people planning events with hospitality venues so they can book a private event as easily as a dinner reservation.
lead_investors: Capital Q Ventures, NEXUS Luxury Collection, T-Squared Social
expansion_signal: Says funds will support entry into new markets (unspecified).
africa_use_case: Event planners in Lagos, Accra and Nairobi could pay venue deposits in local currency through a booking flow, a common pain point for celebrations and corporate events.
notes: New York-based, founded 2026, $16M post-money valuation. Filler-quality lead: the marketplace is US hospitality-focused and expansion markets are not named.

name: Betterness
product: AI health and wellness platform with a voice-first AI life coach (Bett-i) that links consumers to local gyms, providers and wellness brands, plus operating software for wellness businesses.
lead_investors: An unnamed private investment group with pharmaceutical expertise
expansion_signal: Expanding into physical neighbourhood wellness networks, starting at Miami Worldcenter (local, not international).
africa_use_case: Urban African professionals could subscribe to the AI coaching layer and book partner gyms and wellness studios with one wallet payment.
notes: Miami-based. This $1M extension brings total seed to $3.5M; the original $2.5M seed was announced in April 2026 (out of window). The current focus is hyper-local, so this is a weak lead.

name: Heylist
product: Influencer-marketing platform focused on nano and niche creators: AI creator search (built with Mila), campaign management and a new 'Community' feature for brand-run creator programmes.
round_amount_usd: CAD 3.1M (about USD 2.2M; conversion is an estimate)
expansion_signal: Growing across North America and expanding into Europe, starting with the United Kingdom.
africa_use_case: African consumer brands and SMEs could pay to find and run campaigns with local nano-influencers, and payouts to African creators are a natural Cozzipay hook.
founders: Vicky Boudreau, Alexandre Borgia, Nico LeBlanc
notes: HQ is Montreal, Canada, outside the US/UK focus but with no African focus. Brands it has served include L'Oreal and KitchenAid (Seedtable), so its customer base leans toward larger brands. Other investors: Accelia Capital, Investissement Quebec (Fonds Impulsion), The51, Anges Quebec.

name: Dalet Labs (Scene)
hq_country: Not found (Scene launched as an invite-only US app)
product: Scene, an iOS shopping app with an AI-generated visual feed of lifestyle scenes featuring real products from many brands, purchasable through one in-app checkout.
pricing_model: Free app; users make one-off product purchases through a unified checkout.
africa_use_case: Fashion and home-decor shoppers in Nigeria and Kenya who discover US brands on social media could check out in one click with local-currency wallet funds instead of a dollar card.
notes: CAVEAT: the round was announced in window (2026-10-28, first reported by Business Insider), but Business Insider says the pre-seed was raised in late 2025. SV Angel and angels also took part. HQ city not confirmed in the sources read. The app is invite-only in the US, and cross-border shipping limits near-term Africa demand.

name: Vikk AI
product: Consumer AI legal assistant that answers plain-language legal questions, analyses and drafts documents, and matches users with attorneys; law firms buy sponsored placements (Lawyer Ad Center).
pricing_model: Not found (revenue appears to come from law-firm advertising; no consumer price published in the sources read)
lead_investors: Not found (strategic angels including tax attorney Ronson Shamoun and injury attorney Joe Samo)
africa_use_case: Small African law firms could buy sponsored placement to reach diaspora clients asking AI legal questions about immigration or property at home, though the product is US-law focused today.
notes: Long Beach, California (TheSaaSNews; FinSMEs). The $4.2M combines a $3.5M seed with a $700K pre-seed that closed in August 2025. Weak fit, added as a spare in case the duplicate Heylist entry is dropped.
